structured_output.analysis: The budget is full: avg_bits 3.14795 against 84617/26880 bits. Every upgrade therefore has to be paid for with a downgrade. In the retrieved layers, the knapsack already uses the lowest-KL method at each bit width. The only improvement left there is raising the bit width: 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 → rht_gptq_int3 0.00181, 27.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00572 → gptq_int4 0.00217, and 27.gate_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00499 → rht_gptq_int4 0.00153. The cheapest ways to pay are the tabled o_proj downgrades, each predicted to cost about 1e-5 to 4e-5. One 3.1M-parameter MLP layer costs about 1 bit per weight more, so each MLP upgrade is funded by two 2M-parameter o_proj downgrades. The measured KL (0.436) is higher than the predicted 0.398, so interactions matter. I also propose a free, options-only act_order test.

All three are paid for with six o_proj downgrades from the tabled moves.
